q: You and another car reach an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or lights) at the same time. The other car is on your right. Who goes first?
a: The car on your right
w: You do, because you're on the left
e: Same time at an uncontrolled intersection: the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
s: if you arrive at the same time, the vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way

q: At an intersection with no signs or lights, another car got there before you. Who goes first?
a: The car that arrived first
w: You, if you're on the right
e: Yield to a vehicle that approached the intersection before you.
s: At an intersection without signs or lights, you must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle approaching the intersection before you

q: At an all-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
a: The first vehicle to come to a complete stop
e: First to stop, first to go.
s: At an intersection with stop signs at all corners, you must yield the right-of-way to the first vehicle to come to a complete stop.

q: At an all-way stop, you and a car on your right stop at the same time. Who goes first?
a: The car on your right
e: Same time: the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
s: If two vehicles stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right

q: At an all-way stop, you and a car on your LEFT stop at the same time. Who goes first?
a: You do: the car on the left must yield to you
e: Same time: left yields to right. You are on its right, so you go.
s: If two vehicles stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right

q: The traffic lights are out because of a power failure. A car is already in the intersection. What do you do?
a: Yield to it, then go when it's your turn, as at an all-way stop
w: Go through, since you're on the main road
e: Dead lights: yield to vehicles in the intersection and to those entering from your right.
s: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles in the intersection and to vehicles entering the intersection from your right.

q: You're turning left on a green light. An oncoming car is going straight through. Who goes first?
a: The oncoming car
w: You do, because your light is green
e: When turning left, wait for approaching traffic to pass or turn.
s: If you are turning left, you must wait for approaching traffic to pass or turn and for pedestrians in or approaching your path to cross.

q: You're turning left. Pedestrians are crossing the road you're turning onto. What do you do?
a: Wait for the pedestrians to cross
w: Turn, since your light is green
Turn quickly before they reach your lane
e: Yield to pedestrians in or approaching your path.
s: If you are turning left, you must wait for approaching traffic to pass or turn and for pedestrians in or approaching your path to cross.

q: You're turning right on a green light. A pedestrian is about to cross the road you're turning onto. What do you do?
a: Wait for the pedestrian to cross
w: Turn; the pedestrian must wait for you
Turn behind the pedestrian while they're still crossing
e: When turning right, wait for pedestrians in or approaching your path.
s: If you are turning right, you must wait for pedestrians to cross if they are in or approaching your path

q: You're about to turn right. A cyclist is coming up behind you in the bike lane on your right. Who goes first?
a: The cyclist: check your blind spot and let them pass before turning
e: Check your right blind spot for cyclists before you turn right.
s: You should also check your blind spot for cyclists approaching from behind, particularly in a bike lane to your right

q: You face a yield sign. A car is coming on the road you're entering. Who goes first?
a: The car on the other road
w: You, if you got to the sign first
e: Yield = slow down or stop if needed, and let traffic in the intersection or on the other road go first.
s: A yield sign means you must slow down or stop if necessary and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or on the intersecting road.

q: You're pulling out of a driveway. A person is walking along the sidewalk across the driveway. What do you do?
a: Stop and let the pedestrian pass
e: Entering a road from a driveway, yield to vehicles on the road AND pedestrians on the sidewalk.
s: When entering a road from a private road or driveway, you must yield to vehicles on the road and pedestrians on the sidewalk

q: You and an oncoming driver are both waiting to turn left at the same intersection. How do you turn?
a: Each driver turns to the left of the other, after yielding to pedestrians and oncoming traffic
w: Whoever arrived first turns; the other waits
Each driver turns in front of the other
Neither may turn until the light turns red
e: Opposite left-turners pass driver side to driver side.
s: When two vehicles coming from opposite directions meet in an intersection waiting to turn left, each should turn to the left of the other after yielding the right-of-way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

q: A city bus in a bus bay starts flashing its left-turn signal to pull out. You're in the lane next to it. What must you do?
a: Let the bus re-enter traffic
w: Speed up to pass it first
Honk to let it know you're there
e: You must allow a bus leaving a bus bay to re-enter traffic.
s: you must allow the bus to re-enter traffic

q: Two roads going the same way join into one. Who is responsible for merging safely?
a: Drivers on both roads, equally
w: Only drivers on the ending road
Only drivers on the through road
e: Merging is a shared job.
s: Drivers on both roads are equally responsible for seeing that traffic merges smoothly and safely.

q: You're facing a flashing green light and want to turn left. What about the oncoming traffic?
a: They face a red light, so you may turn left
w: They also have a green, so you must yield
They have a flashing yellow, so you must wait
They may turn right in front of you
e: Flashing green = advance green: oncoming traffic still has a red.
s: This is called an advanced green light because oncoming traffic still faces a red light.

q: A pedestrian started crossing on a walk signal. The orange hand appears while they're still in the road. Who has the right-of-way?
a: The pedestrian
w: You, as soon as the hand appears
You, if your light is green
e: Pedestrians already crossing still have the right-of-way over vehicles.
s: While they are crossing, pedestrians still have the right-of-way over vehicles.

q: At a transit priority signal (white vertical bar), who must yield?
a: Other traffic and pedestrians must yield to transit vehicles
e: The white bar gives buses and streetcars their turn.
s: Traffic and pedestrians must yield to public transit vehicles at a transit priority signal.

q: Road work blocks your lane and no one is directing traffic. A car is coming from the opposite direction. Who goes first?
a: The car coming from the opposite direction
w: You, because your lane is blocked
e: Yield to the driver coming from the opposite direction, then go carefully around the obstacle.
s: If your lane is blocked and no one is directing traffic, yield to the driver coming from the opposite direction.

q: You're about to enter a roundabout. A car is already circling inside it. Who has the right-of-way?
a: The car already in the roundabout
w: You, if you're on the right
e: Traffic in the roundabout has the right-of-way. Look left and wait for a gap.
s: Traffic in the roundabout has the right-of-way.

q: You have a green light. An ambulance with its siren on is coming toward the intersection. What do you do?
a: Pull to the right and stop; the ambulance goes first
w: Keep going, since you have a green light
Stop in the middle of the intersection
Speed up to get out of its way
e: Emergency vehicles with lights or sirens always get the right-of-way. Pull over and stop.
s: you are required to bring your vehicle to an immediate stop

q: You're not sure whether you or the other driver should go first. What should you do?
a: Let the other driver go first
w: Go first so they know your intention
e: If in doubt, yield the right-of-way.
s: If you're in doubt, let the other driver go first - yield the right-of-way.

q: What must a driver do before entering a highway from a private road or driveway?
a: Yield right-of-way to all vehicles approaching on the highway.
w: Enter or cross the highway as quickly as possible.
Sound horn and proceed with caution.
Give hand signal then take right-of-way.
e: Official MTO sample question. Drivers coming out of a driveway must wait.
s: When entering a road from a private road or driveway, you must yield to vehicles on the road

q: How many main types of intersections are there, according to the handbook?
a: 2: controlled and uncontrolled
e: Controlled = lights or signs. Uncontrolled = no signs or lights.
s: There are two main types of intersections: controlled and uncontrolled.

q: Which statement about signalling is TRUE?
a: Signalling does not give you the right-of-way
w: Once you signal, others must let you in
You only need to signal if a car is behind you
e: Signal, then make sure the way is clear before you move.
s: Remember, signalling does not give you the right-of-way. You must make sure the way is clear.

q: On a main road, the intersection ahead is blocked with traffic. You must stop before entering and wait. This rule does NOT apply when you are…
a: Turning left or right
w: Going straight on a green light
e: Going straight, don't block the intersection. The rule doesn't apply to turning vehicles.
s: This does not apply if you are turning left or right.

q: Which of these intersections is UNcontrolled?
a: One with no signs and no traffic lights
w: One with stop signs on every corner
e: Uncontrolled = no signs or lights. Be extra careful there.
s: Uncontrolled intersections have no signs or traffic lights.

q: You're coming up to a green light that has been green for a while. What should you do?
a: Be prepared to stop when it turns yellow
w: Speed up to make it through
e: A "stale" green may turn yellow soon.
s: If the light has been green for a while, be prepared to stop when it turns yellow.

q: As you come to an intersection, where should you look?
a: The roadways, and also the sidewalks and paths/trails for pedestrians and cyclists
e: Children may not know the rules, and cycling on the sidewalk may be allowed by local bylaw.
s: Be sure to scan any sidewalks and paths/trails as well as the roadways.

q: What must you do at a yield sign?
a: Slow down or stop if necessary, and let traffic in the intersection or on the other road go first
w: Always come to a complete stop
Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Stop only if a police officer is there
e: Yield = let them go first. Stop only if you need to.
s: At a controlled intersection where you face a yield sign, slow down or stop if necessary and wait until the way is clear before driving through the intersection.
